clue.text: Smear gold and black under bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces for gold and black sit beneath the word for bottom

parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or sea
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone smears gold paint and black onto their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' means placed below, so AU and B follow BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to plaster or spread messily, and the BE- prefix makes it thorough, so it is a synonym of smear.

clue.text: Hindu festival's become larger, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Hindu celebration is said to have grown in size.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mela is a Hindu fair or religious gathering, held at a sacred site.

clue.text: Expect a charge, so watch out for deceit!

definitions.meaning: the warning sign on a field gate means a beast may rush at you
bull is slang for nonsense or lies, so this is a warning against being fooled

explanation.walkthrough: The 'so' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign telling walkers a horned animal may rush them, and also a jokey warning against falsehood, since bull means rubbish talk.

clue.text: I'm a person into piercing — how low can you go with it?

definitions.text: how low can you go with it?

indicators.note: the words for I'm and a person go inside the word for piercing

parts.note: lancing a boil is piercing it
I'm without its apostrophe
a bod is informal British slang for a person

explanation.surface: Someone keen on body piercing is challenged to see how low they can go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How low can you go?' is the traditional chant as the bar is lowered in this Caribbean dance. BOD is British slang for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: In this dance the performer bends backwards under an ever lower bar, the crowd chanting about how low they can go.

clue.text: Radio entertainer speaks of naked clergy?

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase is spoken, so a word sounding like it is wanted

parts.note: knickerless parsons are vicars with no underwear on, said quickly

explanation.surface: A broadcaster talks about clergymen with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Parsons was a British comedy presenter, longtime host of BBC Radio 4's panel game Just a Minute; 'knickerless' (without knickers, British for underpants) said quickly sounds like his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a famous British broadcaster who chaired a Radio 4 comedy show for over fifty years.

clue.text: Offensive force that's friendly with a bit of backbone

parts.note: a warm welcome is a friendly one
a chine is a cut of meat containing the backbone, or the backbone itself

explanation.surface: An attacking unit that is amiable but still has some spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' and 'with' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon or military apparatus used to attack an enemy, hence an offensive force.

clue.text: Asian newt's half asleep, legless

indicators.note: only the first half of the word newt is taken, its first two letters
legless is British slang for very drunk, so the letters of asleep stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A newt lies dozing, unable to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' (British slang for drunk) shuffles ASLEEP into PALESE, after NE, the first half of newt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nepal, the Himalayan country, is a native of Asia.

clue.text: Footballer missing header, opening not finished for team

indicators.note: the famous player's name loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer

indicators.note: the word for opening loses its final letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening for air or gas

explanation.surface: A footballer who fails to head the ball leaves an unfinished gap in his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing header' cuts P from PELE to give ELE; 'not finished' cuts T from VENT to give VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has that many players, so the number stands for a team.

clue.text: Unpleasant chap, I reversed into chum, showing temper

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the word for chum

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: the words for unpleasant chap and I are read backwards together

parts.note: git is British slang for a nasty man

explanation.surface: A nasty man forces his way into a friend's company and loses his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' turns GIT + I into ITIG, which goes 'into' MATE. 'Showing' is a link word. GIT is British slang for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it, a synonym of lessen its severity.

clue.text: I am into girl, rolling over tongue

indicators.note: the whole assembly is turned end to end, read backwards
the words I am go inside the girl's name

parts.note: Cara is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be in love with a girl, rolling over to her side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' puts IAM inside CARA after the C, giving CIAMARA; 'rolling over' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and this is the ancient Semitic language spoken in the time of Jesus.

clue.text: Wiggle targeted, nice butt!

indicators.note: to wiggle is to wriggle about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admires a shapely bottom swaying past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wiggle' shuffles the letters of TARGETED NICE. 'Butt' looks like the bottom being admired; it is the stub of a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is the stub left over once a smoke has been finished.

clue.text: Old kingdom's border, one being constricted?

indicators.note: being here means existing within, so the border and one sit inside the snake

parts.note: with the question mark, constricted points to a boa constrictor, the snake that squeezes
a hem is the border of a garment
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient realm's frontier is being squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic step: whatever is constricted is wrapped in a boa, so HEM and I go inside BOA. The 's is a link for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia was a medieval kingdom of central Europe, now the core of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Implored to secure bird with curved pins

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the word for implored holds the bird inside

parts.note: begged means implored
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded to keep hold of a bird with bent legs.
explanation.walkthrough: PINS is slang for legs, so 'curved pins' are bent legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins is slang for legs, and bandy legs that bow outwards are curved ones.

clue.text: We cut tail off only in primates beginning to struggle, having no arms

indicators.note: the shortened word for only goes inside the word for primates

parts.note: apes are primates

indicators.note: the last letter of the word only is removed
only the first letter of struggle is taken

explanation.surface: We trim a tail and lock primates in, as they start a disarmed struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut tail off' makes ONL from ONLY, which goes 'in' APES; 'beginning to' gives S from struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms here are weapons, so having none means being unarmed.

clue.text: First of codes put in to draw money

indicators.note: the first letter of codes is placed inside the word for draw

parts.note: to lure is to draw or entice

indicators.note: only the first letter of codes is taken

explanation.surface: The first line of a program is entered so as to make some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually with a hint of greed, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Be very scared of aliens, for free to regenerate

indicators.note: regenerating means forming anew, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A science-fiction viewer is terrified of aliens that regenerate for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To regenerate' shuffles OF ALIENS FOR FREE; the surface hints at science-fiction aliens who regenerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in terror that you may be killed is a strong form of being frightened.

clue.text: Boldness shown over eccentric queen, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word for boldness is placed above the word for eccentric

parts.note: face means cheek or nerve, as in having the face to do something
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: Someone acts brazenly towards an odd monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' shows the queen is one example: king and jack are others.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the queen is a court card showing a figure, as are kings and jacks.

clue.text: Thicken with hard material

parts.note: to clot is to thicken, as blood or cream does
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something becomes denser when mixed with a tough substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth is woven fabric, the material clothes are made from.

clue.text: Asian returning east, sent to pinch western idea, gutted

annotationWithheld.clue: Asian returning east, sent to pinch western idea, gutted

clue.text: Head off serious figure

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for serious is removed

parts.note: a weighty matter is a serious one

explanation.surface: A grave number loses its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' takes the W from WEIGHTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure means a number, and this is a number in the tens.

clue.text: Quality party in mind

indicators.note: the party goes inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care
Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: A good characteristic is having a celebration on your mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to care.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre is a degree of excellence or worth, a synonym of standard.

clue.text: Withdraw support for little bird

parts.note: to go is to leave or withdraw
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: Someone stops backing a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is a small, immature bird.

clue.text: Traitor gets one back

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
ago means in the past, back in time

explanation.surface: A betrayer is repaid in kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' is a link word. 'Back' looks like returning something; it means in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello, who betrays his general.

clue.text: Reddish-brown fish taking stock

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A russet-coloured fish counts what is in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking stock' looks like doing an inventory; stock here is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing cattle or horses is the criminal sense, so taking livestock unlawfully.

clue.text: Articulate dark man

indicators.note: to articulate is to say out loud, so the word for dark is spoken

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day

explanation.surface: A well-spoken shadowy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective describing the man; it is the verb to pronounce. 'Man' is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess each piece is called a man, and this one moves in an L-shape.
